title: Error codes
text: Error codes Every diagnostic code Oska reports, with a program that fails with it and the same program fixed. oskac explain <code> prints an entry offline. All of them are in codes.json as data. - E0200: Unknown name "x" with a \ in it, as in Strng - E0201: A trait <script>alert(1)</script> where a type is expected - E0140: An or-pattern such as A B - P0004: Division by zero, see Tests

title: E0200
text: E0200 Unknown name "x" with a \ in it, as in Strng. See the tour. Machine-applicable fix: Replace the name with the closest one. Example This program fails with E0200. fn f(x: Strng) {} Fixed The same program, fixed. fn f(x: String) {} Listed in the checker notes. oskac explain E0200 prints this entry offline.

title: E0201
text: E0201 A trait where a type is expected. Then more. Machine-applicable fix: none. Example This program fails with E0201. fn show(x: Display) { let note = "\"quoted\"" } Listed in the checker notes. oskac explain E0201 prints this entry offline.

title: E0140
text: E0140 An or-pattern such as A B. Machine-applicable fix: none. Listed in the checker notes. oskac explain E0140 prints this entry offline.

title: P0004
text: P0004 Division by zero, see Tests. Spans the operation. Machine-applicable fix: none. Listed in the runtime notes. oskac explain P0004 prints this entry offline.
